lifecycle.note: Explicit 2026 instants. This pilot deliberately has no annual recurrence rule: a 2027 Halloween is a new entry with its own dates, reviewed on its own. The window straddles the Nov 1 DST transition, so both stamps are resolved with the Eastern offset actually in effect on their own date.

typography.heading: brush-display
typography.note: An approved key, never a font-family. It resolves in digest/holidayThemeSchema.js to Knewave, which is already packaged in render/assets-v2/fonts/ under the SIL OFL and already carries an @font-face rule in every artifact. It reaches large decorative brush labels only.

themes.paletteNote: An approved palette key, never a colour. It resolves in digest/holidayThemeSchema.js to HOLIDAY_PALETTE_SPECS['halloween-ambient'], which carries the reviewed day and evening values and is audited for readability, opacity, completeness and ownership separation before it can reach CSS. Adding a future holiday palette is deliberately a reviewed code change: a palette authorable by typing hex into this file would be production-authorable, and every one of those properties would then rest on whoever typed it.
themes.note: First Holiday Theme pilot, revised one controlled step stronger. This entry is purely declarative: it selects one palette key, one typography key and three doodle keys, and authors none of their underlying values. Purple is deliberately absent from the approved palette: purple is already Ophelia's ownership cue and must not become ambient decoration. The palette sets decorative ground, paper, structural borders, brush artwork, brush lettering and one restrained highlight — it cannot reach owner, urgency, warning, weather, status or countdown colours, because those roles are not in the palette spec at all.
